Field semantics (consolidated contract §6/§7; umbrella continuations 92/93):

- `execution profile` — one of `model-free-check` / `baseline-reproduction` /
  `bounded-discovery-probe`; paper-scale profiles never appear in this ledger.
- `split role` — `discovery` or `dev`. `confirmatory` rows require Stage-3 paper authority
  (`OWNER_GO_AND_PAPER_EXECUTION_CONTRACT`) or a dated owner allowance and do not occur in Stage-2.
- `split identity hash` — SHA-256 over the exact sample-identity list this touch may read.
- `consumed` — `yes` only when confirmatory results were read; **irreversible once `yes`**;
  model-free and discovery/dev rows write `no`.
- `inherited exposure` — scoped statement of prior exposure carried into this touch;
  monotonically non-decreasing across rows.
- `calls` / `speech audio seconds` / `gpu hours` — the registered budget record for this
  run; every cell must be a **finite non-negative number** (the gate refuses NaN or
  negative cells outright — they would corrupt the arithmetic). These columns carry no
  numeric ceiling of their own (the first-slice caps that used to sum them as slice
  totals — consolidated contract §6 — were retired by the 2026-08-06 owner amendment,
  `SAEA-OWNER-AMENDMENT-2026-08-06-BUDGET-CAPS`): `contracts.FrozenCoreGate` no longer sums
  these columns across rows. What it still enforces, per row, is the cross-check that a
  plan may only claim what its OWN matched row registers: `registered ≥ planned` for each
  of the three columns, against the plan's own declared `planned_model_calls` /
  `planned_speech_audio_seconds` / `planned_gpu_hours`.

**2026-08-09 second amendment to the SAEA-E-002 rows (before any result is read).** The first launch of the `nocontext` arm ABORTED at slice 575/610 (attempt `attempt-20260809T090531Z-96ccb8`, 577 calls / 34,452 audio-s metered): the llama-server lost its CUDA context mid-run (process alive, 0 MiB GPU) and every later request hung to the 900 s transport ceiling; the bounded per-slice retry fired and also hit the dead server, so the attempt failed closed as designed. Cause: VRAM headroom — `-c 32768 -np 4` reserved 8k KV per slot against slices that need ~1.5k, leaving ~500 MB free on a 24 GB card. Fix attempt 1 (protocol-bound, new config hash): `-c 16384` (4k/slot). **That fix was itself WRONG and was stopped after 81 calls / 4,860 audio-s (attempt `attempt-20260809T112222Z-30ca91`, left OPENED when the operator killed it deliberately, before any result was read).** Reason for stopping: measurement showed the ConEC evidence materials the matched/mismatched arms inject run to 23.3 KB (~5,835 tokens; median 7.4 KB ≈ 1,850), so a worst-case evidence request needs ≈7,000 tokens — more than the 4,096/slot that `-c 16384 -np 4` provides. Letting it run would have completed the no-evidence arm and then failed the two evidence arms, invalidating the whole paired set (all three arms must share one config hash). A systematic memory strategy is being measured instead (KV quantization, CPU-RAM KV fallback using the 43 GB of idle system memory, partial layer offload, and a stable-prefix prompt ordering so a call's evidence block is prompt-cached once rather than re-sent per slice); all three arms then re-run together under one new hash. Both aborted/stopped attempts' spend stays on record here. **2026-08-09 third stop (before any result read): the first final-config attempt of the `nocontext` arm was killed at 86/610 slices after a 7.3× throughput collapse — first quarter 9.9 s/slice, last quarter 72.1 s/slice.** Cause: an ops agent's diagnostic process took a ~715 MiB CUDA context beside the run (it had assumed `-dev none` prevents a context; it does not), squeezing free VRAM to ~350 MiB; with `-ngl 999` disabling llama.cpp's device-memory fitting, allocations spill to host memory under pressure and are never migrated back, so throughput stayed degraded for 12+ minutes after the competing process died. Scientifically the outputs are unaffected (memory placement does not change arithmetic), but at 72 s/slice the three arms would have taken 30+ h instead of ~5 h, so the sequence was restarted on a verified-empty GPU (0 MiB, 0 compute apps). Standing rule adopted: **no process that can open a CUDA context may run beside a live experiment, diagnostics included.** **2026-08-09 fourth stop — a PROTOCOL DEFECT, not an environment one (before any result read):** the clean-GPU rerun of `nocontext` aborted at 581/610 with the same `[100054] asr … timed out`, and the earlier attempt aborted at 577 — a deterministic failure at ~578±3 on a specific input, with all 579 preceding slices healthy (15–16 s each, the last one 3.9 s). Root cause: **the model config declared no generation cap**, so a degenerate slice (silence/music/applause at a call's tail) can run away and generate until the 12,288-token slot fills — ≈600 s at ~20 tok/s — which exceeds even the 900 s transport ceiling, so the bounded per-slice retry could not help either (the retry would burn another 900 s the same way). Fix, protocol-bound and therefore a new config hash: `max_tokens: 1024` in `decoding_params` (≈4–5× the observed 146–250-token slice output, so legitimate transcripts are untouched) and `timeout_seconds` 900 → 240 (≈15× a healthy 16 s slice), which makes a runaway cost ~50 s and lets the retry actually recover. All three arms restart together under the new hash; every aborted attempt's spend stays on record above. **2026-08-09 correction to the fourth-stop diagnosis (recorded before the rerun's results are read).** Log forensics on `attempt-20260809T171603Z-1c09ee` confirmed part of the account above and falsified part of it. Confirmed: exactly one asr invocation never returned (580 `ability_start` events against 579 `ability_end`), and the arm aborted the instant that invocation's retry budget was exhausted. Wrong: it is **not** "a deterministic failure at ~578±3 on a specific input". The two aborted attempts hung on *different* samples (`4366429` in `96ccb8`, `4387383` in `1c09ee` — each attempt wrote 9 of the 10 per-sample derivation files, missing exactly the sample that hung), and the slice ordinal is incidental because `obs_batch_samples: 4` runs four samples concurrently. Nor was anything degrading: across all 580 requests the longest start→end gap was 38.6 s, and the run spanned 1.87 h, not the ~9 h a naive reading of the call count suggests. The fix stands and its rationale is strengthened: with no `max_tokens`, llama.cpp decodes until the slot's 12,288-token context fills, and because decoding is deterministic (temperature 0, fixed seed) the single bounded retry re-sent a byte-identical request and hung identically — **a bounded retry can only recover *transient* failures, never content-deterministic ones**, so capping generation is what actually makes the worst case finite. Consequence for reading the rerun: a slice whose completion is exactly 1024 tokens is a saturation flag rather than a transcript, and must be counted and reported, not scored silently.

**2026-08-09 amendment to all three SAEA-E-002 rows above (before any result is read).** The arms now run: (i) on the **INT4 model** `qwen3-omni-30b-a3b-instruct-gguf-q4km` (model fragment `qwen3-omni-llamacpp-q4km`, runtime receipt `docs/receipts/runtime-q4km.json` sha256 `7be32a78…`) — same switch, same justification and declared limitation as the SAEA-E-001 row; (ii) under the **obs-agent-loop protocol on the openJiuwen batch executor** (baselines `bare-core-ojw` / `fixed-legal-context-ojw` / `mismatched-evidence-ojw`, `obs_batch_samples=4`), so a call is many 60 s slice requests rather than one whole-call request; (iii) on the **mini sample** `r4-e21-sub10` — a seeded 10-of-44 subset of the frozen e21 discovery split, receipt `docs/receipts/probe-samples/r4-e21-sub10-sample.json`, bound into `configs/probes/manifest.json` under the sample-once policy (the rows' split identity hash is the MINI subset's run-identity hash 744c4b2e2d2eece3b05c68089c02000e38c96d5c62db8055d9c421fd509a8f61, because the gate requires the row to name exactly the sample set the plan will read; the parent 44-id discovery split fcc1b0bc55432d02347dcdf730c6bcef561a9b0ad9605c45b367e1ed3da5d69e remains the provenance of that subset and is recorded here in prose. The first chained R4 launch was REFUSED by contracts.gate_exposure on exactly this mismatch, before any model touch). Budget cells raised to the same 2000 / 150000 / 30.0 envelope as SAEA-E-001 to cover slice-level metering; the pre-registered success criterion is unchanged.

The same log shows llama.cpp refusing to size the model to the device: `common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 999, abort`, with 23,406 of 24,462 MiB resident (95.7 %) and the server's own prompt cache climbing past 1,559 MiB against an 8,192 MiB limit. Hypothesis under test (owner's): decode is memory-bandwidth-bound, so any spill of weights or KV to host memory collapses it — the same mechanism already recorded here on 2026-08-09, when one competing 715 MiB CUDA context cost 7.3× and did not recover. **Probe:** four serving configurations — (A) current `-c 49152 -np 4 -fa on -ngl 999 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`; (B) A with `--no-mmproj-offload`, which returns the mmproj's 2,940 MiB worst case to host memory; (C) f16 KV at `-c 32768`; (D) B+C combined — each serving a handful of identical requests built from ONE already-derived discovery slice (`derived/obs-slices/…/4330115/i0000.wav`), measured on the server's own reported prefill/decode timings. Discovery split only; no confirmatory identity is touched; the probe reads throughput numbers and VRAM, never transcript quality. **The R4 sequence was deliberately stopped mid-`matched` to free the GPU for this**, so that arm's partial spend stands on record and all three arms re-run afterwards under whichever configuration wins — serving args are inside the config hash, so this necessarily invalidates the already-completed `nocontext` attempt for pairing purposes and it re-runs too.

**2026-08-11 SAEA-BENCH-featcache correction (before any score was read).** The first COLD attempt was deliberately stopped at 52 slices and is INVALID: the pre-registered "cold run must show no hits" reading caught **382 false cache hits** — `mtmd_input_chunk_get_id` returns the BITMAP-level hash, shared by every ~104-token chunk cut from one audio buffer (~7.4 chunks per 60 s slice), so after the first chunk back-filled, every later chunk of the same slice "hit" and was injected with the FIRST chunk's features. The poisoned cache directory was purged; the key now includes the chunk's prompt position (patched build `862effd0f`, receipt regenerated, diff refreshed at docs/patches/2026-08-11-mtmd-feature-cache.diff; reuse contract unchanged for identical prompts — cold/warm, same-arm repeats — and cross-arm position drift deliberately misses, media-ordinal refinement deferred). The aborted attempt's spend (~52 calls / ~3,100 audio-s) stands on the row; the cold/warm pair restarts under the fixed build.

**2026-08-11 SAEA-BENCH-featcache cold/warm read-out — benefit NOT yet realized; both causes located (results read; `consumed` stays `no`).** COLD attempt `2afd8f` COMPLETED: 19.4 min / 102 calls / WER 0.2310 / **0 hits** (key fix verified) / 806 features back-filled — and vs the unpatched fixedwindow reference (2a0d08: 20.0 min / 0.2316) the patch's cold overhead is ~zero. WARM attempt `0b7e9f` COMPLETED: **20.1 min (no wall gain), 483 hits / 323 encodes (60% hit rate), WER 0.2461, transcripts not byte-identical to cold.** Causes, read directly from the numbers: (1) **position-keyed cache entries break under tail-length drift** — the rolling tail's token count varies with transcript noise across runs, shifting every audio chunk's prompt position (fixed windows removed the AUDIO cascade; the tail still carries a TEXT cascade) — fix: key by media ordinal within the bitmap, invariant to text prefix length; (2) **the 9p mount tax** — features on /mnt/e cost ~per-hit reads that roughly cancel the encode savings — fix: cache dir moves to ext4 (mlruns precedent for performance-critical local state). Honest revision on record: the recoverable ceiling on this arm is 10–29% of wall, pending clean next-round data on how serial encode truly is under 4-way batching. Verdict: NOT lockable; one fix round (ordinal keys + ext4 dir, new build/receipt/config hash) re-runs the pair. Spend added: ~204 calls / ~12.1k audio-s across the two attempts (plus the earlier invalidated 52-call cold).

**2026-08-12 SAEA-BENCH-featcache FORENSICS CLOSED — the collision was one off-by-one (no model touch; log + source forensics only).** Round-3's structure, read from the cold log: each 60 s slice is EIGHT ~104-token media chunks; per request exactly 5 encodes + 3 false hits at the even ordinals. Root cause, verified against source: `find_next_media_chunk` is `upper_bound` (STRICTLY greater), and the ordinal scan advanced by `start + n_tokens` — landing exactly ON the next chunk's start and skipping it, so even ordinals collapsed onto the preceding odd ones and o2/o4/o6 were injected with o1/o3/o5's features (~26 s of each slice heard the wrong audio → WER 0.57). Round-1's ~7.4 false hits/slice (bitmap-only keys, 8 chunks one key) closes under the same model. **Fix build `5d9dfcb58`** (receipt updated in this commit): the one-line advance fix plus a VALIDATE mode (`LLAMA_MTMD_FEAT_CACHE_VALIDATE=1`, fragment q4km-featcache-validate): the hit short-circuit is disabled, everything encodes, and every re-encountered key is byte-compared against the cache — a mismatch logs loudly and is overwritten with encoder truth. **Endgame trio pre-registered under this row:** VALIDATE-1 (populate + intra-run self-check), VALIDATE-2 (full-coverage compare; **806/806 MATCH and 0 MISMATCH is the constructive proof that the cache serves correct features — the owner's "WER 对齐" question answered by construction**), then a clean warm (validation off, full hits) whose wall against the cold reference is **the measured efficiency gain under correct supply — the owner's question 2**. WER of every run is additionally judged against the fixedwindow reference 0.2316/0.2310.

**2026-08-12 SAEA-E-002 R4 n=10 read-out — the paired criterion is NOT met, and the negative control earned its keep (results read; discovery rows stay `consumed=no`; analysis JSON at docs/checks/speech-aware-evidence-acquisition/r4-context-dose-comparison.json).** All three arms COMPLETED+FINALIZED under locked A′ in one sequence (613/608/611 calls; saturated-and-quarantined 2/2/5). Corpus WER: nocontext **27.12%**, matched **24.36%**, mismatched **24.60%** (macro 25.93/24.21/24.54). Pre-registered contrasts (exact Wilcoxon two-sided + 10k-resample bootstrap, seed 20260807): matched−nocontext mean **−1.7 pp**, CI95 [−4.5, +1.0], p=0.375 — direction holds, not significant; **matched−mismatched −0.33 pp, CI [−1.2, +0.5], p=0.557 — NO separation from the negative control**; mismatched−nocontext −1.4 pp, CI crosses zero. **Verdict: the success criterion (matched < nocontext AND matched < mismatched) FAILS on its second leg. The ~1.5 pp benefit of a context block is CONTENT-INDEPENDENT at this dose/form — deranged other-call ConEC lists help as much as the right call's lists.** This is the outcome the design's own caveat anticipated (ConEC materials are unigram frequency bags, and a deranged bag still carries generic earnings-domain vocabulary): the measured value is DOMAIN PRIMING, not call-specific facts. Steers, recorded: (i) E-003/B-2a's form contrasts gain priority (does form unlock call-specific value?); (ii) the self-supplied glossary path (L3) sharpens — if generic domain text is worth ~1.5 pp, a call's OWN accumulating vocabulary may be worth more at zero leakage; (iii) any claim about "evidence quality" on this carrier must first beat the domain-priming floor the mismatched arm now defines. Spend: 1,832 calls / 109,233 audio-s / ~7.5 gpu-h across the three rows this pass.

Wall 19.7 min vs 19.0–20.1 across cold/reference runs: the efficiency gain is ZERO.** Secondary metrics: gpu_seconds 919/899→859 (−5%) and latency_total −6% — the skipped encode shows up per-request but the 4-way schedule absorbs it entirely; decode saturates the device and inline GPU encode was never on the critical path (the serving bench's +3.2 s/slice was the CPU-encode stall, a different mechanism). **Verdict: the feature-cache line closes — the owner's question 1 answered (off-by-one ordinal collapse fed wrong features), question 2 answered by the cleanest possible measurement (with correct supply, ~0 wall gain at -np 4 on this workload). Directional (n=3, single run, fast-split bias caveat as ever); the wave1-sub5 confirmation + a same-config repeat (determinism byte-compare, free) is the natural next pair before any baseline re-registration builds on this. Spend: 102 calls / 6,035 audio-s / ~0.4 gpu-h.

This is the second independent confirmation of the closed-set output contract after A1'r, and it extends it: the contract survives a prepended four-demo block and survives a maximally skewed one, so the ENTIRE FS-SKEW loss is wrong-label choice and none of it is malformed output. `harness_defect_reasons` empty; flight status COMPLETED with error null; 60/60 rows per arm and 180 distinct (arm, sample_id) pairs; `runtime_prohibited=true` and the suite's own note ("gold-derived; scoring-side only; must never enter a runtime path") travel in verdict.json. **SKEW-CAPTURE ACCOUNTING (the disclosed denominator, now measured for the first time)**: the seeded GLOBAL skew label was **`audio`** (drawn once with zero gold input, because a per-sample "wrong for THIS sample" choice would need that sample's own devel gold at binding time and the research boundary forbids it); exactly **1 of 60** samples has gold == `audio` (`slurp:devel:000115:audio-1495375974`) and is excluded as undefined, giving denominator **59**; capture count **2**, rate **2/59 = 0.0339**. **The 0.0339 is not a small capture, it is NO capture**: FS-SKEW predicted `audio` on exactly three rows and all three are rows the ZERO-DEMO arm already answered `audio` on unprompted (`000115` gold=audio excluded, `009340` gold=play, `011503` gold=play) -- so **incremental capture attributable to the 240 skewed demo slots is 0/59 = 0.0000**, and the marginal says the same without reference to any row: `audio` is predicted **3 times under FS-NONE, 3 times under FS-BAL, 3 times under FS-SKEW**. Four demonstrations of a label in every one of 60 prompts moved that label's predicted marginal by ZERO. **The degradation is real but is NOT prior-parroting**: FS-SKEW loses 4 and gains 0 against FS-NONE (strictly one-directional), and **none of the four losses went to `audio`** -- two went to `general`, the catch-all, whose marginal rises 1 -> 2 -> 3 across NONE/BAL/SKEW (`005359` datetime->general, `008072` calendar->datetime, `009733` play->general, `011654` recommendation->transport). A maximally skewed four-shot prior therefore costs about 4 samples in 60 (CI above zero) and buys the skewed label nothing: **the classic ICL label-prior-bias failure mode did NOT reproduce; a smaller generic ICL-noise failure mode did.** This is the label-level companion to P-TRAP's 0/32 cross-sample content-level control -- two independent probes, two exact zeros, on the registration's founding premise that the word-level resonance law does not extend to the label level. **PER-SAMPLE TABLE**: the full 60-row three-arm table (sample_id, gold, per-arm label and correctness) is `per_sample` in `docs/checks/speech-aware-evidence-acquisition/2026-08-19-pfew-read/verdict.json` and is rendered verbatim in that directory's `report.txt`; it is not duplicated in the ledger. Two structural readings drawn from it. (i) **The primary null is a WASH, not stillness**: FS-BAL and FS-NONE tie at 49 but agree on only 54 of 60 labels, differing on 6 with an exact **3 gains / 3 losses** split (gains `005025` music->iot, `008047` lists->calendar, `009518` news->play; losses `000943` datetime->qa, `009733` play->general, `012478` transport->takeaway); balanced demos move 10 percent of the population and move it in both directions equally, acting as a RE-RANDOMIZATION of borderline decisions rather than as information about the label space (all three arms identical on 51/60). (ii) **The residual error is one confusable cluster, not diffuse noise**: `play` accounts for **6 of the 11** zero-demo errors and collapses into its media neighbours (3 -> `music`, 2 -> `audio`, 1 -> `news`), scoring 1/7 on FS-NONE, 1/7 on FS-BAL and 0/7 on FS-SKEW, while **9 of the 18 canonical classes are perfect on all three arms**; more than half the available headroom therefore sits in a single systematic confusion that generic demonstrations provably cannot address, which is the concrete reason the +0.10 gain was never in reach. **UNREGISTERED DESCRIPTIVE, NO CLAUSE ATTACHED -- IN-SESSION REPLICATION DISCREPANCY**: the in-session FS-NONE comparator reads **49/60 = 0.8167** where the cited consumed A1'r phase-1 read **47/60 = 0.7833** on the SAME 60 samples, with a pre-flight-verified BYTE-IDENTICAL prompt block (`pslu-s2-a1r-phase1-closed-set-v1`, 432 chars), the same decode config (`-c 49152 -np 4 -fa on -ngl 999 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`; temperature 0, seed 20260803, max_tokens 1024), the same split identity hash and the same runtime build and GGUF hashes. **Dataset analysis fixes the information requirements and the next cold engineering cell before model contact.** SLURP train contains 11,514 sentences, 50,628 real recordings, 18 scenarios, 91 fine-grained intents, 46 action values, 60 observed scenario--action pairs, and 55 entity types. At recording weight the scenario prior entropy is 3.944 bits; conditioning on action leaves 1.091 bits, and conditioning jointly on action plus the observed entity-type signature still leaves 0.611 bits. Therefore operation cues alone are information-incomplete: speech-conditioned target/object/context evidence remains necessary. The frozen knowledge artifacts cover all 18 scenario definitions and all 60 scenario--action pairs through 18 target plus 60 operation factors; every card has five train-only positive examples and a contrastive boundary. However, only 30 explicit graph boundaries cover 66 cross-scenario pairs sharing an action, leaving a legitimate knowledge/AgentLoop optimization surface rather than evidence that speech failed. **The next M11 prompt optimization is implemented model-free as a versioned policy, without adding a script or model contact.** Policy `speech-conditioned-adaptive-evidence-gap-v2` reuses the existing matcher and contact dispatcher while moving deterministic graph knowledge into the llama.cpp JSON grammar: one `oneOf` branch per candidate binds `key_id` to only that key's registered factors, and `prefixItems` requires the first factor to be an operation. The local pinned llama.cpp source at commit `04ccc72a2` implements both constructs. The v1 policy remains readable and reproducible; the existing experiment config now points prospectively to v2. This removes the observed cross-key/operation structural degree of freedom without adding an information-free retry. The reranking handler requires a string query, string documents, rank pooling, and a reranker-compatible model; it cannot accept the registered speech-feature packet and is not available from the current always-on Omni profile. Generated-token logprob and reranking therefore remain outside the M11 state and training-free action space. Reconsideration requires a receipt-pinnable speech-query-to-fixed-key conditional sequence score on the same decoder-only service, with no second model or profile replacement. Manager PID 612 / server PID 620 were not contacted, stopped, or modified.

Four further gates had to pass first and did: the flown retain-versus-dispatch decision is reproduced per sample (100 of 100, 100 of 100, 400 of 400, **497 of 500**) and the three NEW500 deviations are **exactly the three v2 delta-override fires** `002303`, `002955` and `014737` with zero unexplained, which is the expected consequence of replaying the LOCKED v1 cell against an arm that flew v2; the flown SUPPLY is reproduced exactly on every dispatched sample (37, 33, 130, **163**); the DEV-100 committed reports' own retain-primary and correct counts are reproduced (63 and 72, 67 and 72); and **every direct-decode text this gate tokenizes re-hashes to the `text_sha256` its own landed query-vector record carries, 1,100 of 1,100** - so the lexical channel's query side is byte-identical to the dense channel's, and no text can have been substituted for another. 9,900 vectorised cosines were cross-checked against `kb_policy._cosine` and all agreed to 1e-9.

**THE FALSIFIER, EVALUATED AS WRITTEN AND NOT REPAIRED AFTER THE ANSWER.** The agenda plan pre-registered 'if hybrid ranking does not raise recall at 5, key representation is not the lever either, and the residual is task-intrinsic'. On the primary unexposed 500 - the population the lock statistic used - recall at 5 rises from **0.744 to 0.762 under RRF at k=60 (+1.8 pp, +9 of 500)** with the raw direct-decode query text, and to 0.758 with the schema-key-stripped variant; on NEW400 it rises 0.715 to 0.735. **The antecedent is NOT met, so the falsifier's conclusion is NOT licensed: the key plane is not saturated, and a channel that has never been used reaches gold facets the dense channel misses, consistently across two disjoint held-out populations.**

**AND THE FLIGHT IS STILL REFUSED, on three quantities the falsifier did not name and this gate measured anyway.** (1) Every rule that raises recall at 5 COSTS recall at 1: the same RRF-60 takes the unexposed 500 from 0.636 to 0.590, minus 23 samples at the head of the list, and the z-normalised linear rules degrade monotonically in the lexical weight (recall at 1 falls to 0.384 at w=0.75). (2) The already-measured conversion anchors are steeply rank-dependent - 98.2 percent at fused top-1, 69.6 percent at fused rank 2 or 3, 0.0 percent absent - so demoting one gold from rank 1 costs 0.286 expected correct answers while promoting one from absent buys 0.696, and 23 demotions against 9 promotions does not close. (3) With the second dimension ACTUALLY ACTIVATED inside the registered `kb_policy` ranker and fuser at the frozen tau 0.65 / m 5 / c 2 / top_l 3, the supply newly carries gold on **12 currently-wrong trajectories and LOSES gold on 40 currently-correct ones** (12 against 29 under the stripped query; 11 against 21 and 9 against 13 on NEW400) - the loss side exceeds the gain side on every population under both query normalizations by a factor between 1.4 and 3.3. **The central conversion projection is NEGATIVE everywhere: minus 2.70 pp and minus 0.75 pp on the unexposed 500, minus 1.82 and minus 0.77 on NEW400, minus 1.83 and minus 1.49 on DEV-100 rounds 4 and 5.** No trajectory anywhere was priced at the unanchored rank-4-plus extrapolation, because the frozen top_l of 3 keeps every priced sample inside the measured anchor set.

**A REGISTERED DEFECT IN THE FALSIFIER'S OWN CONSTRUCTION, recorded rather than used as licence to reinterpret the result.** A single-sided recall test cannot see a cell whose top-1 conversion is 98.2 percent, where the head of the list is worth more than its tail. Any future key-plane falsifier on this cell must be two-sided - recall at 1 AND recall at 5, or the conversion-weighted quantity 0.982 times P(rank 1) plus 0.696 times P(rank 2-3) directly. Read against that objective every rule in the grid is a loss, which is the same verdict the projection reaches independently.

**THE STRUCTURAL RESULT THAT STANDS AND IS THE ONE DURABLE ASSET.** The plan's section 2.1 degeneracy is CONFIRMED on all 1,100 samples before it is repaired - `dims_total` 3, every facet carrying exactly one dimension, `agreement` the constant one third, the score the affine map 0.5 cos plus 0.0667. With the lexical dimension live, `dims_total` becomes 4, **`agreement` takes two distinct values (one quarter and one half) instead of one**, 293 of 2,500 top-m candidates on the unexposed 500 carry `dims_hit` equal to 2 (**11.7 percent**, rising to 13.5 percent under the stripped query and to 14.3 percent on NEW400), 181 to 217 of the 500 samples carry at least one two-dimension candidate, and **1,417 facets were percept-admitted by the lexical dimension ALONE** with a dense cosine below the tau bar. At the frozen `w_agree` of 0.2 the separation between a two-dimension and a one-dimension candidate at equal maximum signal is **0.05, equivalent to a plus 0.10 cosine bonus**. **The rank-weight family is structurally non-degenerate for the first time.** That is a true statement about the score's SHAPE and is independent of, and survives, the negative accuracy projection; it is explicitly NOT a claim that re-weighting now buys accuracy.

**COST NOTE, MEASURED NOT MODELLED, AND IT CORRECTS THE PLAN IN THE USEFUL DIRECTION.** The lexical channel is FREE: under the registered scoring form every per-document BM25 weight is query-independent, so the index over all 11,514 content-facet texts is built ONCE in **0.054 s** (5,219 terms, 78,402 postings, corpus sha256 `4b971c1a...3da1`) and a query is a gather plus a bincount costing **9.64e-5 s = 0.096 ms**, i.e. **0.096 s per 1,000 trajectories against the plan's 2,294 s per 1,000 reference - a factor of 4.2e-5**. The plan's engineering note reads 'any second dimension multiplies that 1.147 s'; it does not. The 1.147 s belongs to the EXISTING scalar cosine sweep in `kb_policy.multidim_recall`, and this module's vectorised equivalent measures **0.98 ms for the same 11,514-facet sweep - a roughly 1,170-fold speedup whose fidelity the 9,900-probe agreement check already proved**. Vectorisation is therefore NOT a prerequisite blocker for K1; it is a demonstrated small change worth landing on its own merits for the roughly 19 minutes of CPU per 1,000 trajectories it removes from every future campaign.

**WHICH TIER COULD EVALUATE IT, VERIFIED AGAINST THIS GATE'S OWN NUMBERS RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** Against the registered plus-or-minus 2 per 100 variance channel: DEV-100 sees a central effect of minus 1.8 samples against plus-or-minus 2 (**cannot resolve**, confirming the plan's statistical-honesty clause); NEW400 sees minus 7.3 against plus-or-minus 8 (**cannot resolve**); the unexposed 500 sees minus 13.5 against plus-or-minus 10 (**marginal at best**). The plan said 'NEW400-tier or larger'; **that is too generous, and the honest floor is at least 1,000 samples** - which, with a negative central sign, is not worth spending. Note the asymmetry in what carries variance: the retrieval numbers are exact arithmetic over sealed query vectors and carry no decode variance whatever, and only the projected accuracy does.

STAGE G1 IS STOPPED AT THE GATE, BEFORE ANY FLIGHT, BY THE RULE THIS ROW FIXED IN ADVANCE.** Row `SAEA-SN-MF-A2T-G1-PROMPT-FIT-NP8` (registered `11d2ec2d` BEFORE any contact), generator `scripts/a2t_g1_prompt_fit.py` (committed `545cfc27` before that), receipt `docs/checks/speech-aware-evidence-acquisition/2026-08-25-a2t-g1-prompt-fit/prompt-fit.json` sha256 `fd1edfa1d7fc6aa852775d368865237a24d3033f7c56f92e6ab7752d24ea69c6` with its README stating the outcome verbatim. **THE NUMBERS, EXACT FROM THE RESIDENT TOKENIZER, NOT ESTIMATED.** Envelope `m0-direct-decode` renders **13,236** text tokens; envelope `blend-evidence-decode-worst` renders **19,047**. Against the locked np8 profile's **8,192** tokens per slot (`-c 65536 -np 8`, verified live at preflight as `/health` ok with 8 of 8 slots idle) the margins are **-10,921** at the locked 64-token completion reserve, **-11,881** at the A2T-required 1,024-token reserve, and **-12,395** once a realistic 514-token speech allowance is added. Required context per slot **20,587** against **8,192** available: the requirement is **2.51 times the budget**. THE HEADLINE IS THE M0 ARM, NOT THE EVIDENCE ARM: M0 carries no evidence slot at all - it is the bare prompt-matched direct decode that produced the published A0 comparator - and it overruns a slot by **5,046 tokens while being credited with ZERO audio tokens and ZERO output reserve**. The BLEND overrun (10,857 on the same zero-credit basis) is a consequence, not the cause. The frozen registry is 50,291 characters and is counted exactly ONCE (`task_contract_counted_once` true), so no double-rendering inflates this.

**THE PRIMARY BOUND CREDITS ZERO SPEECH TOKENS ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS WHY THE RESULT IS SAFE.** Audio2Tool has no promoted speech-feature packet root (the prior A2T flights encoded audio live through the mtmd feature cache `/home/chao/feat-cache/audio2tool-q4km`, 490 legacy `.feat` entries, no packets), so no packet could be measured without first flying a preprocessing pass. Zero is the strictly MOST GENEROUS assumption available and can only help the prompt fit, so a negative margin computed at zero speech tokens is a **LOWER BOUND on the deficit** and cannot be an artefact of the assumption. The 514-token secondary applies the landed np8 SLURP receipt's own measured rate (117 tokens at 8.126875 s, 78 at 5.312 s, about 14.4 tokens per audio second) to this carrier's longest item `tier7_multiturn:001590` at 35.714 s; it is a reference and was never the gate.

**THE CAUSE IS SERVING GEOMETRY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, AND THE COMPARATOR ALREADY KNEW IT.** llama-server divides `-c` across `--parallel` slots, so the locked profile yields 65,536 over 8 equals 8,192 per slot - a geometry sized for SLURP, whose ENTIRE BLEND evidence prompt measured **6,174 against that same 8,192 slot at margin +1,954**. Audio2Tool's BARE REGISTRY CONTRACT is larger than SLURP's whole evidence prompt: 13,236 against 6,174, a factor of **2.14**, on a task contract of 50,291 characters against 5,424, a factor of **9.3**. The registered A0 flight's own committed launcher records that it dropped its fragment's `-np 4` to `-np 1` - the whole 49,152-token context to one sequence - PRECISELY because `-np 4` would have given 12,288 per slot, 'BELOW this flight's own ~12.6k-token registry prefill'. **A0 could not fit its own prompt at 12,288 per slot; the locked profile offers 8,192.** A0's own estimate was additionally an UNDER-estimate: the exact count is 13,236, not the ~12,693 the binding config projected, because dense JSON punctuation tokenizes more finely than a chars-over-4 heuristic predicts.

**WHAT THIS IS NOT.** It is NOT evidence that the paradigm fails to transfer: nothing here touches retrieval, fusion, dispatch or decode, and the G0 reachability gate still stands at PASS (lexical ceiling at k=5 0.7925 against A0 tool accuracy 0.5425). The established finding is narrower and purely mechanical - **the locked cell's SERVING GEOMETRY, not its knobs, is physically incompatible with the Audio2Tool contract size, and the paradigm was never given the chance to run.** It is also NOT a licence to shrink, summarize, truncate or retrieve over the 152-row registry: that would move M0 away from the published A0 comparator and silently answer a different question, which the campaign plan section 4.3 forbids. NO KNOB WAS CHANGED and no file under `rails/` or `core/` was touched.

**THE PROJECTION, ARITHMETIC AND SINGLE-VARIABLE.** Per-slot context is `-c` divided by `-np`, so at the unchanged total 65,536 the whole fix is one integer. Requirements including the 514-token speech reference and the 1,024-token completion reserve are M0 14,776 and BLEND-worst 20,587. `-np 8` gives 8,192 and FAILS both (-6,584 and -12,395). `-np 4` gives 16,384 and passes M0 (+1,608) but still FAILS BLEND (-4,203). **`-np 3` gives 21,845 and is the MINIMUM that clears the worst envelope (+1,258); `-np 2` gives 32,768 and is the first setting with real headroom (+12,181)**, leaving total context, KV cache and VRAM unchanged so no memory re-measurement is needed, at a throughput cost of 2 concurrent slots instead of 8. THREE THINGS WOULD HAVE TO BE REGISTERED TOGETHER and none of them is a policy knob: (1) `-np 8` to 2 or 3, a SERVING-GEOMETRY change while alpha, tau, recall top-k, fusion m and c and top_l, rank weighting, prior source, boundary stage and percept admission all stay at the locked v1 cell; (2) `max_tokens` 64 to 1,024, forced by the output shape - a JSON call list, not a single short label - and already the registered A0 value on this carrier; (3) the A2T speech-feature packet root, which does not exist and must be materialized by a label-free preprocessing pass before any arm can fly against a `--no-mmproj` decoder. Whether (1) and (2) forfeit the plan's section 4.1 'transfers-unchanged' claim is an OWNER decision, not this row's: the honest framing available is that they are carrier-forced SERVING parameters rather than tuned knobs, but they are still changes and section 4.1 requires any A2T-specific change to be registered as such.

**SCOPE, BINDING.** This row measured a token bound and evaluated one gate. Per its own preregistered stopping rule the `SAEA-A2T-G1` campaign row was NOT registered, no preprocessing pass was flown, no canary was run and no arm was flown. It authorizes NO flight, NO campaign registration, NO knob change, NO generality claim and NO Stage-3 activity; a generality claim belongs to G2 on the unexposed tier and cannot be reached from anything measured here. **THE DEFECT, MEASURED ON BOTH CARRIERS.** The ranker forms `w_cos * max_cosine + w_prior * max_prior + w_agree * agreement` at 0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2. The agreement term is DEGENERATE on both carriers and cancels exactly - `dims_total` is 3 and every recalled facet carries exactly one dimension, 1,560 of 1,560 on A2T and 7,500 of 7,500 on SLURP - so ranking is decided by `0.5 * cosine` against `0.3 * prior` alone. No content facet ever carries prior mass on either carrier, so that comparison is ALWAYS a cosine against a mass, on two scales. **THE INVARIANT THE LOCKED CELL SILENTLY RELIED ON: every admissible content facet outranks every prior-mass facet if and only if `w_prior * sup(prior_score) < w_cos * tau`, i.e. `sup(prior_score) < 1.08333`.** MEASURED: SLURP sup is exactly **1.0000** (inside, margin **+0.0833**) because `rails.knowledge_build` divides an intent count by its own containing scenario count and the ratio is a genuine conditional probability; Audio2Tool sup is **4.1000** (outside by **3.78x**) because `rails.knowledge_build_a2t` divides a tool count taken across every (domain, category) by one category's count, and tool to (domain, category) is not a function on this corpus - the G0 report's own finding that `tool_id` is not a join key. All ten recalled A2T prior-mass facets carry a mass above 1.19, i.e. every one of them is outside the declared range.

**CEILING A - THE ALPHA VETO IS STRUCTURAL, AND THE BOUND IS ATTAINED RATHER THAN MERELY RESPECTED.** `_fused_label_scores` floors every raw label score at 0.0 before the max and then normalizes, so `fused` lies in `[0,1]` with `sum(fused)` in `{0,1}` BY CONSTRUCTION whatever the ranker returns; `_blend_scores` then gives the direct label `alpha*f + (1-alpha)` and every rival `alpha*f`, so the worst-case margin is `1 - 2*alpha` = **+0.10** at the frozen alpha 0.45 against the `_argmax_labels` tie tolerance of 1e-9. A recovered direct label is therefore the strict unique argmax for EVERY possible supply, and `retain == direct-label-recovered` is a property of the POLICY FORM rather than an empirical finding. THE DEFECT. `SAEA-SN-MF-STAGE2A-MATURED-SYNTHESIS` established from source that BOTH knowledge builders compute `prior_score` as a ratio whose numerator and denominator range over DIFFERENT populations: `rails/knowledge_build_a2t.py:1085-1087` divides a tool's row count taken over the WHOLE construction pool by one `(domain, category)`'s row count, and `rails/knowledge_build.py:696-698` divides an intent's globally-counted rows by a scenario's globally-counted rows. Neither restricts the numerator to the conditioning event, so neither is a conditional probability and neither has any reason to be <= 1; the A2T measured supremum is 4.1 with 193 of 12,601 values above 1, and SLURP is safe ONLY because `intent = f"{scenario}_{action}"` (line 202) makes an intent strictly determine its scenario. (1) It REPAIRS the computation in both builders so the numerator is restricted to the conditioning event - A2T `count(rows with this tool AND this (domain, category)) / count(rows in this (domain, category))`, SLURP `count(rows with this intent AND this scenario) / count(rows in this scenario)` - and renames every local whose name asserts a restriction the code did not perform. | 2026-08-25 | SAEA-SN-MF-FUSION-FORM-OFFLINE-GATE | model-free-check | THE FUSION-FORM OFFLINE GATE - a ZERO-CONTACT projection over ALREADY-SEALED records deciding whether the facet ranker's THREE-KINDS-IN-ONE-SUM scoring form is worth proposing as a change, computed before any line under `rails/`, `core/` or `configs/` is touched and computed WITHOUT touching one. THE QUESTION: `rails/kb_policy.py`'s registered ranker sums `w_cos * max_cosine + w_prior * max_prior + w_agree * agreement` into ONE score, and the three summands are quantities of DIFFERENT KINDS - a cosine is a similarity, `max_prior` is a probability mass, `agreement` is a coverage fraction. The field's standard practice is to keep one comparison on one bounded scale, and the literature's three canonical answers to incommensurability are (i) convert similarities to a distribution and interpolate it with a second distribution (kNN-LM, Tip-Adapter), (ii) normalize each list then combine, and (iii) fuse RANKS rather than scores (reciprocal-rank fusion). THE CANDIDATE CHANGE UNDER TEST: the facet ranking score becomes COSINE ONLY, and the prior moves to the layer where it is ALREADY a probability - `_fused_label_scores`, which normalizes to sum 1 and is then interpolated by `_blend_scores` - which is the kNN-LM / Tip-Adapter shape and which also removes the `agreement` term's established constant-one-third degeneracy. WHY THIS IS ASKABLE CLEANLY ONLY NOW: the prior-score semantics repair (`docs/readiness/2026-08-25-prior-score-semantics-repair.md`, commits `b3a420d7` / `ea77413c`) made `prior_score` a genuine conditional probability on BOTH carriers - corrected supremum exactly 1.0, priors summing to 1 over every conditioning cell - so the question is no longer confounded with that defect. WHAT IS COMPUTED, all of it arithmetic over sealed bytes, with the REAL `kb_policy.multidim_recall`, the REAL registered fuser, the REAL `_fused_label_scores` / `_blend_scores` / `_argmax_labels` imported so that ONLY THE SCORING DIFFERS between arms: (C0) the CONTROL, the live form exactly as landed, which must reproduce the flown decisions as a FAIL-CLOSED fidelity gate before any other arm's number is read; (C1) COSINE-ONLY facet ranking with tau, k, m, c and top_l unchanged, so the prior dimension no longer competes for the top-m window; (C2) C1 plus the prior as a LABEL PRIOR entering `_fused_label_scores` MULTIPLICATIVELY on the raw label score before normalization - the Bayes / Tip-Adapter frequency-weighted-cache shape, parameter-free, introducing NO new knob - with a secondary registered comparator C2B that instead INTERPOLATES the retrieval distribution against the prior distribution at a pre-registered lambda grid 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.50, the literal kNN-LM shape, reported as a comparator only because it introduces a knob that is not in the frozen table; and (C3) RRF ACROSS DIMENSIONS at K=60, the literature's third answer, carried as a comparator with the K1 gate's own measured result quoted beside it (RRF-60 raised gold-facet recall-at-5 0.744 to 0.762 while LOWERING recall-at-1 0.636 to 0.590 and was REFUSED for flight on exactly that basis). A form must not reduce the number of dispatched trajectories that receive a non-empty supply, and must not reduce the aggregate number of distinct supplied task_targets or the aggregate number of supplied values on the dispatched set. (2) Mirroring the published protocol genuinely improves tool selection: on the SAME 400 rows, the SAME official metric and the SAME official gold, with each cell parsed by the contract it was built to emit, 55.50 -> 61.00, delta +5.50 pp, 54 saves / 32 harms / 314 ties, sign test p 0.0230, CI90 [+1.75, +9.25] pp. Summed per-tier gap to the paper falls from 116.3 pp to 77.3 pp. (3) Tier 1 moves the WRONG WAY: 66.0 -> 60.0 under the correct protocol, against a published 92.4, with a 100 % parse rate and an exact match of 12.0 against the paper's 92.4. Tier 1 is now the single unexplained quantity; seven tiers sit between -12.6 and +3.4 pp. (4) The a2t-toolcall and a2t-toolcall-v2 columns are 0.0 with 400 parse failures each -- a FORMAT mismatch, not a model result, since those scorers parse the reconstructed JSON-array contract. The paper-facing number is a2t-toolcall-official throughout. Mechanism work stays stopped; the open question is now whether the paper's Tier-1 row comes from a first-speaker-per-query population this roster does not represent, or from a candidate tool set narrower than all 152 -- an owner decision. No superiority, generality or Stage-3 claim; exposed discovery data; no knob tuned on it. |

THE EXTENSION CONTINGENCY DOES NOT FIRE: the remaining 1,646 tier-1 queries are not flown. Exact match 10.20 % [8.18, 12.64] against a published 92.4; parameter F1 14.40 macro / 1.20 micro; parse rate 100.0 %; zero rows named more than one call. THE SUBSTANTIVE FINDINGS. (1) The roster is worth +5.6 pp, not +32: the frozen 400's own 50 tier-1 rows score 60.00 [48.4, 70.6] under the same scorer, so drawing the release's own population moved the number a little and mostly bought resolution -- at n = 50 the CI90 spanned 22 points. (2) At n = 500 the tier splits by DOMAIN and the split is the whole story: wearables 93.41 % [87.75, 96.55] on n = 91 and smart_car 92.68 % [83.04, 97.04] on n = 41 both sit ON the published 92.4, while smart_home -- 368 of the 500 rows -- sits at 55.71 % [51.42, 59.91]. Equal-domain weighting gives 80.60 % against the natural mixture's 65.60 %. There is no general Tier-1 problem on this runtime. (3) The named component, a diagnostic that enters no decision: 161 of the 163 smart_home misses name ANOTHER REAL TOOL of the 152-row registry (only 2 invent a name); 79 stay inside smart_home and 82 pick the same idea's twin in smart_car. The top confusions are rebootDevice->restartDevice (12), setSecurityMode->armSecuritySystem (8), activateScene->activateRoutine (7), setColor/setColorTemperature/setLighting->setAmbientLighting (17 together, the last of those a smart_car tool), getAirQuality->getAirQuality_diag (5). The failure mode is near-synonym selection inside a registry that contains near-synonyms, and the domain ranking follows the count of confusable neighbours exactly. (4) Exact match remains the sharper anomaly and is not a scoring artefact: of the 328 rows that pick the right tool, 277 attach an argument the argument-free tier-1 gold does not have, and the extended a2t-toolcall-v2's default-argument credit lifts EM only to 14.60 %. Two of the three ranked suspects are now closed; quantization is the only one still open. No superiority, generality or Stage-3 claim; discovery data; no knob tuned on it. |

The instruction STRING is byte-identical to arm B's, sha256 8533f771edf09f036aa333ed9631e531e5a0c4493efa5f7b0f53fdcf751154d6, so the only thing that varies between B and C is where that string sits. THE SEAM, deviation H2: one new request-shaping config key omit_system_message on core.model.transport.LlamaServerTransport, beside the user_turn_text and user_turn_audio_first keys the 2026-09-04 Audio2Tool official-protocol work already added. It travels in config_hash to protocol_hash like every other request-shaping key and DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so every fragment that predates it renders byte-identical requests, which tests/unit/test_llama_server_transport.py pins directly on the sealed A/B arms. rails.task_adapter.TaskAdapter.assemble_prompt is UNCHANGED; no probe module, no TaskAdapter subclass, no controller subclass, and scripts/checks/engineering_base_check.py passes. The seam is fail-closed because its failure mode is silent: the transport refuses omit_system_message without a declared user_turn_text, under any speech-feature prompt order, for a non-bool, for any request whose payload task_instruction is not byte-identical to the configured user_turn_text, and for any request carrying evidence or an exemplar bank. EVERYTHING ELSE IS HELD: same roster, same media bytes, same reference layer, same scorers, same build, same geometry, same decoding params, same harness, same entry point scripts/flights/run_e22_esb_cell.py. SCORING: the manifest declares asr-wer-esb-whisper, asr-wer-esb and cost, scored once through core.scoring_batch as one whole-manifest job, never sharded, over the same hash-pinned dev10 reference layer; references never enter the request path. Paid API spend 0. DECISION RULE, preregistered: if arm C's pooled corpus Whisper-normalized WER beats arm A AND the paired C-minus-A CI90 lower bound is above 0 AND the hypothesis-to-reference length ratio falls toward 1.0, the official usage shape becomes this study's ASR request shape for cleaned-reference protocols and the verdict RECOMMENDS TO THE OWNER a second and final read of the six ESB test calls under shape C, which the owner alone may authorize and which this flight never flies; otherwise the shape is EXCLUDED and the remaining suspects, context-free clipping, decoding length control and quantization, are named for the owner without being flown. NO ALIGNMENT VERDICT IS ISSUED: no published number covers these ten dev calls, and whether arm C's dev figure would sit inside the 3-point band of the published 9.79 or the cross-read 12.3 is reported as an INDICATION ONLY. No superiority, generality or Stage-3 claim; no mechanism arm; no test tuning; no paper-scale work CONSUMED 2026-09-05: COMPLETED and FINALIZED, attempt attempt-20260905T094322Z-2174df, study commit a402f6281777ca27f8178904e3fe1258c2f1b8b9, config hash b9e14e330360d9ea6a1478e2677837af6973562e6341cd8c8052c9749d1e7436, protocol hash b75c42cb4120589cab293f264305c043a3881df82d871fbe42badb60e73e6e13, manifest sha256 a7d304eee2e85cb2e4bd5cacb9808f7aec1fa5e91733b5faf8c39dffc34341a0. All 6038 of 6038 utterances, 39292.64675 speech seconds (10.915 h), 6038 of 6350 registered calls, 1652.1 s of dispatch at eight slots plus 11.1 s of server startup = 0.4620 GPU-h against a 1.0 registered and 0.6 planned ceiling, 23.78x realtime, mean latency 2.074 s, 3.655 contacts per second, one attempt with no recovery, no CUDA fault, no out-of-memory and no skipped contact. RESULT: corpus WER under the Whisper EnglishTextNormalizer is 17.8896 percent over all 6038 utterances against arm A's sealed 17.5648 and arm B's 18.3944, so arm C is 0.325 points WORSE than the control. Substitutions 4433, deletions 4975, insertions 9094 over 103423 reference words. THE SHAPE DID EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS PREDICTED TO DO TO THE LENGTH AND THE NUMBER STILL GOT WORSE: the hypothesis-to-reference length ratio fell 1.0861 to 1.0398, insertions fell 11270 to 9094 and their share of all errors fell 62.04 to 49.15 percent, but deletions rose 2370 to 4975, about 1.20 deletions for every insertion removed, and total errors rose 18166 to 18502. The two aggregations disagree in sign and both intervals exclude zero: the paired per-utterance delta C minus A on negated WER is +0.01819 with CI90 [+0.0112, +0.0251] (arm C better, 1436 saves / 1537 harms / 3065 ties, sign test p 0.0666) while the corpus-level delta is -0.3249 points with CI90 [-0.5297, -0.1160] (arm C worse), because arm C wins every duration bucket under 4 s and loses every bucket above 8 s, and rows under 4 s are 35.6 percent of the roster but only 13.4 percent of the corpus denominator. THE ORACLE BOUND MOVED THE WRONG WAY, which is the real result: an oracle cut of each hypothesis to its own reference word count takes arm A to 10.697 (-6.868) but arm C only to 12.273 (-5.617), 1.58 points HIGHER, so the words arm C stopped emitting were words the reference wanted. Over-generation was a symptom, not the cause. One clean win recorded: hypotheses containing CJK-range characters fall from 14 (A) and 12 (B) to 0 (C). Scored once through core.scoring_batch as one whole-manifest verified job, never sharded. THE WINDOW FIT HELD TO THE TOKEN: largest prompt 1045, exactly 13 x ceil(78.36) = 1027 speech tokens plus the 18-token envelope, against a 5120-token slot; largest completion 118 against a 1024 ceiling never reached; and arm C's prompt-token total is exactly 6038 x 5 below arm B's, the five tokens of system-block scaffolding the template no longer writes, on every row. VERDICT: the official usage shape is EXCLUDED and is NOT adopted, and NO second read of the six ESB test calls is recommended to the owner. Two of the preregistered rule's three conditions hold (the paired CI90 lower bound is above 0, and the length ratio falls toward 1.0) but the governing one, that arm C's pooled corpus WER beat arm A, fails. Pooled over the four acceptance tiers (1, 2, 5, 6) the paired Q8-minus-Q4 tool accuracy is +0.50 pp, 4 saves / 3 harms / 193 ties, sign test p = 1.0000, tier-stratified bootstrap CI90 [-1.50, +2.50] pp -- the interval contains zero, so the residual gap to the paper is NOT the decoder quantization. THE SHARPEST FACT: tier 1 is 60.0 % on both decoders with ZERO saves and ZERO harms across all fifty rows, and the `wearables` domain is 72.63 % on both across 95 rows with zero discordant pairs. The one tier that carries the whole unexplained gap, and the one domain that already matches the paper, are exactly the places quantization does not touch. Over all eight tiers there IS a small real effect: overall tool accuracy 61.00 -> 63.25 (+2.25 pp, 16 saves / 7 harms / 377 ties, p = 0.0931, CI90 [+0.25, +4.25]), two thirds of it tier 8 alone (34.0 -> 44.0, 6 saves / 1 harm); under a2t-toolcall-v2 it is +2.50 pp ordered (CI90 [+0.75, +4.50]) and +3.00 pp multiset (CI90 [+1.00, +5.00], p = 0.0227). Per-tier Q8 official tool accuracy: tier1 60.0 (paper 92.4, -32.4), tier2 76.0 (-8.6), tier3 76.0 (+1.3), tier4 30.0 (-3.4), tier5 76.0 (-14.6), tier6 86.0 (+4.5), tier7 58.0 (+3.4), tier8 44.0 (+2.3); exact match 20.50, parameter F1 31.36 macro / 26.96 micro, parse rate 100.0 (the one Q4 parse failure now parses), 66 rows named more than one call. Summed absolute per-tier gap to the paper 77.3 -> 70.5 pp. Against the paper C-q8 is still FAIL under the replication preregistration's own definitions: tiers 1, 2 and 5 outside 5 pp and outside their Wilson CI90, rank order not preserved. Per domain, paired: wearables 72.63 -> 72.63 (0/0/95), smart_car 72.22 -> 77.78 (+5.56), smart_home 55.39 -> 57.99 (+2.60); natural mixture 61.00 -> 63.25, equal-domain 66.75 -> 69.47. THROUGHPUT AND MEMORY: mean latency 6.141 s per call against the resident Q4_K_M cell's 0.782 s, i.e. 7.85x -- not the 4.17x of the August whole-model-offload note and not the 32x the cold-cache 4-row smoke projected; 953.4 s of generation wall at 3 slots, 0.4195 contacts/s, model load 16.0 s, whole flight 17.4 minutes. GPU memory 21,930 MiB of 24,463 with 2,208 MiB free at --n-cpu-moe 24; server host RSS 20,646 MiB of 49,783 MiB available. Prompt tokens 1,464,049 over 400 calls -- IDENTICAL to the digit to the sealed Q4_K_M flight's, which is independent corroboration that the request did not move. Feature cache 5,617 entries before and after with zero encoding lines, so no mmproj encode ran. GPU enforced.power.limit 100.00 W before and after and 0 MiB in use after the server stopped; during generation the enforced limit wobbled 96.8-98.3 W with NO throttle reason active (0x0, SW Power Cap and HW Slowdown both Not Active, 57 C) while the GPU drew about 21 W at 4-12 % utilisation because 24 of 48 MoE layers ran on the CPU -- laptop dynamic-boost arbitration, not the Quiet-mode 35 W collapse, and incapable of binding this workload. CONSEQUENCE: the last controllable model-usage suspect is closed. Suspects now closed by measurement are the reconstruction (-5.50 pp), the system-prompt whitespace variant (+1.00 pp, p = 0.5034), the roster (+5.6 pp at n = 500) and the quantization (+0.50 pp, CI90 containing zero). What remains is the llama.cpp audio front-end against the HF processor, and the published tier-1 row itself, which five separately sealed cells have now failed to reproduce. Q8_0 does NOT become the operating core by this row; that is a separate owner decision, and on 7.85x latency for +2.25 pp pooled and 0.0 pp on tier 1 the Q4_K_M core stands. No superiority, generality or Stage-3 claim; exposed discovery data; no knob tuned on it. |

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cell B1, speech-keyed exemplar supply to the Solver

Cell B1 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-slurp-v2-base-program-design.md` (module M1), on the
cell B0 review-off base, under the A2 decision of
`docs/results/2026-09-17-slurp-a2-exemplar-headroom-audit-v1.md` (plain top-k = 20, sealed Fold A
speech vector as the key, no intent diversification, derangement twin). One factor moves against
cell B0's own configuration: `knowledge_stores` gains one named store, `train-exemplars`, which
supplies the Solver phase with twenty annotated construction-pool exemplars as typed content blocks
on the acquire transition. No instruction byte changes, no contact is added, and two contacts per
row remains the exact program ceiling. The registered twin gives every row another Fold A
recording's sealed speech vector by a seeded within-delivered-scenario derangement, so the exemplar
block is token-matched by construction and the only factor that moves between arm and twin is
whether the speech keying the retrieval is the row's own. Comparators are sealed bytes: cell B0
primary, the anchor secondary; neither is re-flown or re-scored. Readiness stays `held`.

**These six rows are registered before contact and the cell is BLOCKED.** `rails.knowledge_stores.
build_knowledge_store_supply` refuses the configuration outright -- `candidate, explicit, and scoped
supply cannot overlap on phase(s) ['solver']` -- because the `slot-contracts` store already serves
the Solver through `candidate_supply` while `train-exemplars` serves it through `phase_supply`. The
E3 commit `cfdf08fb` added the composition that routes a later-phase plain `phase_supply` into
`automatic_for_phase`, and names this exact pairing in its own module comment, but left the older
collision guard that refuses it and covered only the `context_supply` pairing with a test. The
refusal is inherited, not introduced here: the committed anchor-based
`configs/baseline/slurp-native-dual-store-train-fold-a-exemplars-k20-v1.json` reproduces it
identically. Until a separately reviewed engineering item closes that guard, `check`,
`prepare-supply`, the smoke and the campaign all refuse, `prepared_phase_supply` cannot be pinned,
and no contact of any kind may be opened against these run ids.

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cell B2, sample-and-aggregate commit

Cell B2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-slurp-v2-base-program-design.md` (module M2,
engineering items E2 and E2b), on the cell B0 review-off base, under owner decision 4 of
2026-09-16. One factor moves against cell B0's own configuration, and it is the `episode`-class
switch key `native_episode.roles.solver`: the Solver role declares `samples 5`,
`decoding_overrides {temperature 0.7, seed_offset 0}` and
`commit {policy saea-commit-plurality-support-v1, min_support 3, similarity_threshold 0.8}`. One
Solver visit therefore makes five real distinct-seed contacts through the same metered request path
a single Solver visit uses, and a deterministic commit policy aggregates the five parsed answers
into the one delivered answer. The program ceiling moves from 2 to 6 contacts per row and is exact:
`1 + 1*(0 + 0 + 1*5) = 6`.

The rendered request is proven row for row against cell B0's: on all 1,080 rows and all four
declared phases it differs by exactly the 9-byte phase-program id inside the `[agent control ...]`
marker, for the arm and for the twin alike, with zero rows differing in any other way. The five
sibling Solver requests of one visit differ from each other only by `seed`, and from cell B0's
single Solver request only by `seed` and `temperature` (the twin: only by `seed`). The rebuilt
Perception supply selects identically to cell B0's and the anchor's on all 1,080 rows.

The registered greedy-repeat twin pays the identical six contacts per row and runs the identical
commit policy at temperature 0, so its five drafts differ only by llama.cpp batch-composition
nondeterminism: arm minus twin isolates sampling diversity from the aggregation itself. It is the
only flown control; both comparators are sealed bytes and neither is re-flown or re-scored.
Readiness stays `held` with only the preparation requirement until the coordinator adds the decision
requirement and flips.

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cells B4a, B4b and B4c, the ORG knowledge cells

Cells B4a and B4b of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-slurp-v2-base-program-design.md` (modules
M4a and M4b), plus the added separation cell B4c, all on the cell B0 review-off base and all under
the named fixes of `docs/results/2026-09-17-slurp-a3-coverage-confusion-audit-v1.md`. Cell B4a moves
the standing `general_quirky` Perception fallback candidate (FIX-1) together with the
`intent-boundaries-v2` store revision that carries the one-directional qa/general contrast (FIX-2);
its primary estimand is intent accuracy with pooled SLU as the non-inferiority guard. Cell B4b moves
the `slot-contracts-v2` store revision alone (FIX-4 date emit-when-spoken, FIX-5 time spoken form,
widened to the omission-dominated types); its primary estimand is pooled official SLU micro F1 with
intent as the guard. Cell B4c moves the intent store revision alone, so that an admitted B4a can be
decomposed; it is the lowest-priority cell and carries no smoke of its own.

No contact is added: two contacts per row remains the exact program ceiling on all three cells, and
the modules move knowledge content and the consumption-side candidate list only. The prepared
first-phase Perception supply of every one of the five cells selects the identical facet ids as the
sealed anchor preparation and as cell B0's own artifact, on all 1,080 rows (receipt
`coordination/slurp-b4-org-cells-v1/phase-supply-vs-base-v1.json`). Comparators are sealed bytes:
cell B0 primary, the anchor secondary; neither is re-flown or re-scored.

**These ten rows are registered before contact and every cell stays `held`.** Nothing may fly before
the cell B0 verdict is recorded: B0 is both the base these cells extend and their primary
comparator. If B0 is HARMFUL, the coordinator re-bases all three cells on the sealed anchor and
recomputes every composed hash, protocol hash, plan hash and ledger note in the package first.

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cell B1 on the sealed anchor base (v2 registration)

Cell B1 of the SLURP v2 base program (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-slurp-v2-base-program-design.md`
section 4, module M1), **re-based on the sealed dual-store anchor**. The 2026-09-17
re-decision of module M0 under the TRAIN A own null returned HARMFUL, so the Reviewer/Planner
review loop is retained and every later cell of the program builds on the anchor rather than on
the review-off base. These six rows replace the six review-off rows registered earlier the same
day; those were never flown, stay `consumed = no`, and each carries a supersession note.

One factor moves against the sealed anchor configuration: `knowledge_stores` gains one named
store, `train-exemplars`, which supplies the Solver phase with twenty annotated
construction-pool exemplars as typed content blocks on the acquire transition. Measured before
contact on all 1,080 rows: the rendered Perception, Reviewer and Planner requests are
byte-identical to the anchor's, and removing exactly the twenty `train-exemplars` blocks from
the Solver request reproduces the anchor's Solver envelope on 1,080 of 1,080 rows. No
instruction byte changes and no contact is added; eleven contacts per row remains the exact
program ceiling and about five per row is the expected spend. The registered twin gives every
row another Fold A recording's sealed speech vector by the seeded within-delivered-scenario
derangement, so the exemplar block is token-matched by construction. Comparators are sealed
bytes: the anchor primary, the released direct anchor secondary; neither is re-flown or
re-scored. Readiness stays `held`.

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cell B2 RE-BASED on the sealed anchor (v2 package)

Cell B2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-slurp-v2-base-program-design.md` (module M2,
engineering items E2 and E2b), registered on the **sealed dual-store anchor** under owner decision
6 of 2026-09-17: the B0 re-decision returned module M0 (review loop off) HARMFUL under the TRAIN A
own null, so every later cell builds on the anchor. This package **supersedes before contact** the
review-off-based v1 registration (`docs/readiness/2026-09-17-slurp-b2-samples5-v1-preregistration.md`);
the v1 cells never flew, their six rows stay `consumed = no`, and each carries a supersession note.

One factor moves against the anchor, and it is the `episode`-class switch key
`native_episode.roles.solver`: the Solver role declares `samples 5`,
`decoding_overrides {temperature 0.7, seed_offset 0}` and
`commit {policy saea-commit-plurality-support-v1, min_support 3, similarity_threshold 0.8}`. One
Solver *visit* therefore makes five real distinct-seed contacts through the same metered request
path a single Solver visit uses, and a deterministic commit policy aggregates the five parsed
answers into the one delivered answer. The review loop stays ON (reviewer 3, planner 1,
`max_revisions 1`), so the program ceiling moves from the anchor's 11 to `1 + (1+1)*(1*5 + 3 + 1) =
19` contacts per row, and a Planner `REVISE` re-samples the whole group.

The rendered request is proven row for row against the anchor's: on all 1,080 rows and all four
declared phases it differs by exactly the phase-program id inside the `[agent control ...]` marker,
for the arm and for the twin alike, with **zero** rows differing in any other way. The five sibling
Solver requests of one visit differ from each other only by `seed`, and from the anchor's single
Solver request only by `seed` and `temperature` (the twin: only by `seed`). The rebuilt Perception
supply reproduces the anchor's prepared artifact `output` (SHA-256 `ba5e1faa…`) on all 1,080 rows
and the sealed smoke artifacts' (`512583ec…`) on its 4.

**Registered known behaviour, new on this base.** Agent states are registered per *contact*, so one
grouped Solver visit leaves five separate `kind=phase:solver` states in the episode history: the
Reviewer and the Planner read all five raw samples, not the one committed answer. The commit policy
governs the *delivered* answer only. This is registered rather than repaired — suppressing or
replacing per-contact states is a production change that owes its own engineering item — and its
prompt cost is bounded at under 2,304 extra tokens against the anchor's measured tightest margin of
9,194 tokens.

Both comparators are sealed bytes and neither is re-flown or re-scored. The greedy-repeat twin is
the only flown control and, under owner decision 8, launches only after the arm shows a positive
CI95 against the base. Readiness stays `held` with only the preparation requirement until the
coordinator adds the decision requirement and flips.

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cells B4a, B4b and B4c re-registered on the sealed anchor

Cells B4a and B4b of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-slurp-v2-base-program-design.md` (modules
M4a and M4b), plus the added separation cell B4c, all rebuilt on the **sealed dual-store anchor**
(`configs/baseline/slurp-native-dual-store-train-fold-a-anchor-v1.json`, review loop on) after the
2026-09-17 re-decision of module M0 as HARMFUL under the TRAIN A own null (owner decision 6). The
review-off v1 package of the same three cells is superseded before contact and never flew; its ten
rows stay `consumed = no`.

Cell B4a moves the standing `general_quirky` Perception fallback candidate (FIX-1) together with the
`intent-boundaries-v2` store revision that carries the one-directional qa/general contrast (FIX-2);
its primary estimand is intent accuracy with pooled SLU as the non-inferiority guard. Cell B4b moves
the `slot-contracts-v2` store revision alone (FIX-4 date emit-when-spoken, FIX-5 time spoken form,
widened to the omission-dominated types); its primary estimand is pooled official SLU micro F1 with
intent as the guard. Cell B4c moves the intent store revision alone, so that an admitted B4a can be
decomposed; owner decision 9 of 2026-09-17 makes it conditional on B4a admitting, and it carries no
smoke of its own.

No contact is added: the eleven-contact program ceiling of
`configs/policy/phase-native-candidates-review-revise-v1.json` is the anchor's own, the anchor's
realized cost was 5,417 contacts over 1,080 rows, and these modules move knowledge content and the
consumption-side candidate list only. The prepared first-phase Perception supply of every one of the
five cells selects the identical facet ids as the sealed anchor preparation, on all 1,080 rows and
on the four smoke rows (receipt
`coordination/slurp-b4-org-cells-anchor-v2/phase-supply-vs-anchor-v1.json`). Comparators are sealed
bytes: the dual-store anchor primary, the released direct anchor secondary; neither is re-flown or
re-scored.

**These ten rows are registered before contact and every cell stays `held`.** The margins are the
TRAIN A own-null half-widths measured by cell B0r, h_SLU 1.1218 pp and h_intent 1.0051 pp, not the
imported DEV-1000 margins the v1 package used. Cell B4c must not fly unless cell B4a is ADMITTED.

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cell B2 RE-REGISTERED after E2c (v3 package)

Cell B2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-slurp-v2-base-program-design.md` (module M2,
engineering items E2, E2b and **E2c**) on the **sealed dual-store anchor**. This v3 package
**supersedes before contact** the v2 package
(`docs/readiness/2026-09-17-slurp-b2-samples5-anchor-v2-preregistration.md`); the v2 cells never
flew, their six rows stay `consumed = no`, and each carries a supersession note.

The base, the roster, the one moved factor, the commit thresholds, the comparators, the decision
rule, the budgets and the twin trigger are the v2 registration's, unchanged. What changed is the
harness under them. E2c (merged at `59db0f9b`) makes a grouped Solver visit take ONE step: it
registers exactly one `kind=phase:solver` agent state, carrying the commit policy's aggregated
answer, in the same wire form a samples-1 (anchor) Solver state has. The Reviewer and the Planner
therefore read ONE draft exactly as they do on the anchor, so this cell moves the
sampling-and-aggregation channel alone -- the v2 registration had to register "the Reviewer reads a
sample set instead of a draft" as a second, unmeasured difference. The five raw samples stay in
custody: their own contacts, their own `MODEL_REQUEST`/`MODEL_RESPONSE`/`COST` trace records and
metered cost, one `action_alternatives` wave naming all five with their own response digests, and
the sealed `solver_group` receipt `analysis.native_commit_replay` re-aggregates offline. Because the
group takes no step between its samples, the five siblings see the same `QueryState` -- independent
draws of one draft, not a chain. A Planner `REVISE` re-samples the whole group and re-commits, which
is why 19 and not 15 is the ceiling.

Because a grouped request now carries the anchor's own form, the prompt-fit statement uses the
anchor's measured per-role-visit maxima directly with a one-state bound (tightest `planner:1`,
15,382 required tokens, 9,194 tokens of margin); the v2 four-extra-state growth term is withdrawn.

Proven before contact, model-free: the rendered request equals the sealed anchor's on all 1,080 rows
and all four declared phases after exactly the phase-program-id substitution, for the arm and the
twin alike, with **zero** rows differing otherwise; the five sibling Solver requests differ from each
other only by `seed` and from the anchor's single Solver request only by `seed` and `temperature`
(the twin: only by `seed`); the rebuilt Perception supply reproduces the anchor's prepared artifact
`output` (SHA-256 `ba5e1faa…`) on all 1,080 rows and the sealed smoke artifacts' (`512583ec…`) on
its 4; and a fake-model rendered proof over the four smoke rows shows exactly one `phase:solver`
state in every Reviewer and Planner request, a `REVISE` that re-samples five and re-commits, and a
rendered volume within one character of an anchor-shaped episode scripted with the same answer.

Both comparators are sealed bytes and neither is re-flown or re-scored. The greedy-repeat twin is
the only flown control and, under owner decision 8, launches only after the arm shows a positive
CI95 against the base. Readiness stays `held` with only the preparation requirement until the
coordinator adds the decision requirement and flips.

A Planner REVISE re-samples the whole group and re-commits, which is why 19 and not 15 is the ceiling. Proved model-free by tests/unit/test_native_episode_runner_grouped_solver.py::test_grouped_solver_revise_resamples_and_the_reviewer_reads_the_committed_draft, ::test_grouped_solver_keeps_every_raw_sample_in_custody and ::test_samples_one_solver_state_is_the_raw_draft_the_reviewer_reads, and measured on the four smoke rows by coordination/slurp-b2-samples5-anchor-v3/e2c-rendered-proof-v1.json. The prompt volume is therefore the ANCHOR'S OWN FORM -- one solver state per Solver visit -- so the anchor's measured maxima apply with the one-state bound (tightest planner:1, 15,382 required tokens, 9,194 margin) and the v2 package's four-extra-state growth term is withdrawn. The 12.0 GPU-hour ceiling is the anchor's own registered ceiling, kept unchanged; it assumes the five sibling Solver requests of one visit share their cached prompt prefix on one slot (id_slot per-sample plus --cache-prompt), and the server also runs --no-cache-idle-slots and --slot-prompt-similarity 0, so the assumption is unproven and the measured GPU hours are a mandatory verdict field. ## 2026-09-17 - SLURP v2 cell B1 recovery on the E3c-fixed code (anchor base)

Cell B1's arm `SAEA-SLURP-NATIVE-EXEMPLARS-K20-ANCHOR-TRAIN-FOLD-A-V2` aborted at
2026-09-17T09:52:35Z on the first row whose Planner routed REVISE: the re-entered Solver
re-ran its prepared phase supply, the decision re-selected the same twenty `train-exemplars`
values, and `EvidenceAgentController._acquired_ids` refused them. 84 rows were complete; 420
generation calls and 911.865938 repeated speech seconds are durably spent against that run id,
which is now closed and never re-used. The four-row smoke could not have caught it: all four
rows routed ACCEPT.

The fix is `rails.controllers.restrict_repeat_visit_supply` (commit `f2595f4c`, merged
`cfbb5f8b`): a phase this trajectory has already answered acquires only what its `QueryState`
does not already hold, and every FIRST visit is returned unchanged. These four rows are the one
root-diagnosed recovery re-registration the preregistration section 11 allows for this run.
Nothing else moves: same roster, split, role graph, prompts, knowledge stores, exemplar supply,
speech semantics, caps, geometry and resident session. The registered twin keeps its own
unflown v2 identity and flies on the fixed code only after a positive arm CI95. Readiness stays
`held`. Full statement:
[`docs/readiness/2026-09-17-slurp-b1-exemplars-k20-anchor-v2-recovery-v1.md`](readiness/2026-09-17-slurp-b1-exemplars-k20-anchor-v2-recovery-v1.md).

## 2026-09-17: SLURP v2 base program cell B7a, the Node Context Policy at level L1, on the sealed anchor

Cell B7a of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-node-context-policy-design.md` section 11 (module M5 of the SLURP v2 base program), on the **sealed dual-store anchor**
(`configs/baseline/slurp-native-dual-store-train-fold-a-anchor-v1.json`, review loop on, nominal 5 contacts per row, program ceiling 11). Engineering item E8a merged at `ff668547`;
E8a authorised no cell, and this registration is what opens one.

The moved key is `native_episode.context_policy`, the third key of the closed `episode` switch-class allowlist. ON is level `structured` on exactly the eight model-output
boundaries with `on_parse_failure` `raw` (`refuse` for `solver:plan-action`), the four tool-observation boundaries declared `raw`, and no producer response format. OFF is the key's
absence, which is the anchor fragment itself. Level L2 (`cleaned`) is refused at load time and is cell B7b; the Reviewer response format is B7r; the tool-observation rewrite is B7c.

No contact is added: L1 is a deterministic, zero-contact transform over the already-selected history. Proved model-free over all 5,417 sealed anchor requests through the production
renderer: the Perception request is byte-identical on 1,080 of 1,080 rows; the Solver, Reviewer and Planner differ only in the agent-state parts the policy rewrites (1,100 of 1,110,
4,344 of 6,548 and 2,180 of 5,444 states); 0 of 2,184 tool-observation states change; all 5,417 control envelopes are identical; and every `raw` receipt row's `rendered_sha256` equals
its source's `content_sha256`. The prepared Perception supply of both cells reproduces the sealed anchor preparation's `output` block on all 1,080 rows and the four-row reference on its 4.

**These four rows are registered before contact and both cells stay `held`.** The margins are the TRAIN A own-null half-widths measured by cell B0r, h_SLU 1.1218 pp and h_intent 1.0051 pp.
A NEUTRAL L1 still enters the SLURP default plan, by the design's own rule.
